spec_match.rationale: Runs a real background fetch at a loopback target and, crucially, frames the result against the page's own address space — correctly teaching that loopback-to-loopback crosses no LNA privilege boundary.

interactive.rationale: Start/Clear buttons, capability steps, a context panel and worker-reported record rows; verified a full run end to end via a trusted CDP click.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card promises an attempted fetch that says which case it proves instead of staging one, which is precisely the context panel's job.

edge_cases.rationale: The permission-not-queryable state, the no-boundary loopback case, and worker failures are all distinct explained states rather than assumed successes.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/6225598451154944 and the Local Network Access specification.

conformance.rationale: The suite covers the queryable-permission and targetAddressSpace contracts (honestly failing pre-154), but its background-fetch-requires-user-activation assertion reads FAIL on a fresh profile because getRegistration() finds no service worker — same flawed pattern as the CORS feature's suite; flagged for a human, not edited.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): trusted click ran the whole flow — worker registered, fetch accepted, backgroundfetchsuccess, 1/1 record readable at 127.0.0.1 — and the detail correctly warned this is not evidence about the restriction; permission probe honestly reported not-queryable (TypeError); console clean.

telemetry_health.rationale: Loads demo-telemetry.js and logs each step plus the worker outcome.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables, step states as text plus colour, captioned table, no static card.

accessibility.rationale: Context uses dl semantics, steps carry text beside aria-hidden icons, table has caption and scoped headers, detail is aria-live.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 (scrollWidth 360, screenshot read).

summary: Reviewed at http://localhost:3000/v154/local-network-access-restrictions-for-background-fetch/attempt-a-fetch/ with Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp). A trusted CDP click ran a genuine background fetch to 127.0.0.1 which succeeded, and the page did the epistemically right thing: its context panel identified the page itself as loopback and explained that success here is not evidence about the restriction — no faked failure, no false claim. The local-network permission honestly reported not-queryable on this pre-154 build. Console/network clean bar the sandbox font-CDN artifact; no mobile overflow. Feature /conformance/ ran 4 pass / 3 fail; two fails are honest pre-154 results, but background-fetch-requires-user-activation fails on any fresh profile for lack of a service worker registration rather than a real contract breach — flagged for human review.
